subproblem.title: Gram determinant: det(F*∘F) is the square of the frame-coordinate determinant
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, F : ℝⁿ → ℝᴾ a continuous linear map and τ = (τ₁, …, τₙ) an orthonormal family in ℝᴾ such that F eⱼ ∈ span{τ₁, …, τₙ} for every j, where eⱼ = EuclideanSpace.single j 1 is the standard basis of ℝⁿ. Then det(F*∘F) = (det 𝒜)², where F* is the adjoint of F, det(F*∘F) is the determinant of the endomorphism F.adjoint ∘L F of ℝⁿ (ContinuousLinearMap.det), and 𝒜ᵢⱼ := ⟨τᵢ, F eⱼ⟩.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (F : Euclid n →L[ℝ] Euclid P) (τ : Fin n → Euclid P), Orthonormal ℝ τ → (∀ j, F (EuclideanSpace.single j (1 : ℝ)) ∈ Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range τ)) → (F.adjoint ∘L F).det = (Matrix.of fun i j => inner ℝ (τ i) (F (EuclideanSpace.single j (1 : ℝ)))).det ^ 2
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 3(ii) and 3(iii) of the parent proof (Gram matrix Γ = 𝒜ᵀ𝒜 and det A(v) = det Γ), stated for an arbitrary continuous linear map F and an orthonormal frame τ whose span contains the vectors F eⱼ.
Notation: ℝᵐ means Euclid m = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m); ⟨x, y⟩ is inner ℝ x y; e_j := EuclideanSpace.single j (1 : ℝ) is the j-th standard basis vector of ℝⁿ; an n-covector of ℝᴾ is an element of Covector (Euclid P) n = Euclid P [⋀^Fin n]→L[ℝ] ℝ (a continuous alternating n-linear map ℝᴾ × ⋯ × ℝᴾ → ℝ); MultiVector P n = Covector (Euclid P) n →L[ℝ] ℝ (continuous linear functionals on n-covectors); for a continuous linear map F, F* = F.adjoint and det of an endomorphism is ContinuousLinearMap.det (= LinearMap.det of the underlying linear map). Write bⱼ := F eⱼ and 𝒜ᵢⱼ := ⟨τᵢ, bⱼ⟩.
1. Expansion in the frame. Fix j. Since bⱼ ∈ span(range τ) there are reals cₗ with bⱼ = Σₗ cₗ • τₗ (Submodule.mem_span_range_iff_exists_fun). For each l, orthonormality gives ⟨τₗ, Σₘ cₘ τₘ⟩ = cₗ (Orthonormal.inner_right_fintype), i.e. 𝒜ₗⱼ = cₗ. Hence bⱼ = Σₗ 𝒜ₗⱼ • τₗ.
2. Gram matrix. For all i, j, by step 1 applied to bᵢ and bilinearity (sum_inner, inner_smul_left; real scalars): ⟨bᵢ, bⱼ⟩ = ⟨Σₗ 𝒜ₗᵢ τₗ, bⱼ⟩ = Σₗ 𝒜ₗᵢ ⟨τₗ, bⱼ⟩ = Σₗ 𝒜ₗᵢ 𝒜ₗⱼ = (𝒜ᵀ𝒜)ᵢⱼ (Matrix.mul_apply, Matrix.transpose_apply).
3. Matrix of F*∘F. Let B := (EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin n) ℝ).toBasis, the standard basis of ℝⁿ (Bⱼ = eⱼ), whose coordinate functionals are B.repr(x)ᵢ = xᵢ = ⟨eᵢ, x⟩ (EuclideanSpace.basisFun_repr, EuclideanSpace.inner_single_left). The (i, j) entry of the matrix of the linear map F*∘F in the basis B is (F*(F eⱼ))ᵢ = ⟨eᵢ, F*(F eⱼ)⟩ = ⟨F eᵢ, F eⱼ⟩ (LinearMap.toMatrix_apply, ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint_inner_right) = (𝒜ᵀ𝒜)ᵢⱼ by step 2. So LinearMap.toMatrix B B (F*∘F) = 𝒜ᵀ𝒜.
4. Determinant. ContinuousLinearMap.det is LinearMap.det of the underlying linear map, and the determinant of a linear endomorphism is the determinant of its matrix in any basis (LinearMap.det_toMatrix). Therefore det(F*∘F) = det(𝒜ᵀ𝒜) = det(𝒜ᵀ)·det(𝒜) = (det 𝒜)² (Matrix.det_mul, Matrix.det_transpose). ∎

The following Lean proof was compiled by the parent decomposition session against that frozen import closure (lean 4.35.0-rc3; `#print axioms` = propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound; no warnings) and passes the runtime leaf-delta check `check_source_delta`; it may be used verbatim:
theorem Submission.dgoj_det_adjoint_comp_eq_det_sq : ∀ (P n : ℕ) (F : Euclid n →L[ℝ] Euclid P) (τ : Fin n → Euclid P), Orthonormal ℝ τ → (∀ j, F (EuclideanSpace.single j (1 : ℝ)) ∈ Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range τ)) → (F.adjoint ∘L F).det = (Matrix.of fun i j => inner ℝ (τ i) (F (EuclideanSpace.single j (1 : ℝ)))).det ^ 2 := by
  intro P n F τ hτ hb
  set A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ :=
    Matrix.of fun i j => inner ℝ (τ i) (F (EuclideanSpace.single j (1 : ℝ))) with hA
  have hexp : ∀ j, F (EuclideanSpace.single j (1 : ℝ)) = ∑ l, A l j • τ l := by
    intro j
    obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := (Submodule.mem_span_range_iff_exists_fun ℝ).1 (hb j)
    have hcA : ∀ l, A l j = c l := by
      intro l
      rw [hA, Matrix.of_apply, ← hc, hτ.inner_right_fintype]
    rw [← hc]
    simp only [hcA]
  have hgram : ∀ i j, inner ℝ (F (EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℝ)))
      (F (EuclideanSpace.single j (1 : ℝ))) = (A.transpose * A) i j := by
    intro i j
    rw [Matrix.mul_apply]
    conv_lhs => rw [hexp i]
    rw [sum_inner]
    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun l _ => ?_
    rw [inner_smul_left, Matrix.transpose_apply]
    simp [hA]
  let B := (EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin n) ℝ).toBasis
  have hmat : LinearMap.toMatrix B B ((F.adjoint ∘L F : Euclid n →L[ℝ] Euclid n) : Euclid n →ₗ[ℝ] Euclid n)
      = A.transpose * A := by
    ext i j
    rw [LinearMap.toMatrix_apply, ← hgram i j]
    simp only [B, OrthonormalBasis.coe_toBasis, OrthonormalBasis.coe_toBasis_repr_apply,
      EuclideanSpace.basisFun_repr, EuclideanSpace.basisFun_apply, ContinuousLinearMap.coe_coe,
      ContinuousLinearMap.coe_comp, Function.comp_apply]
    rw [← ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint_inner_right, EuclideanSpace.inner_single_left]
    simp
  rw [ContinuousLinearMap.det, ← LinearMap.det_toMatrix B, hmat, Matrix.det_mul,
    Matrix.det_transpose, sq]
proof_key_steps: Each bⱼ = F eⱼ lies in span(range τ), so bⱼ = Σₗ 𝒜ₗⱼ τₗ with 𝒜ₗⱼ = ⟨τₗ, bⱼ⟩ (orthonormal coefficients).
The matrix of F*∘F in the standard basis of ℝⁿ has entries ⟨eᵢ, F*F eⱼ⟩ = ⟨F eᵢ, F eⱼ⟩, i.e. equals 𝒜ᵀ𝒜.

audit.reason: The frame expansion proves the Gram matrix equals AᵀA; the adjoint identity identifies it with the matrix of F*F. Determinant invariance then proves the exact square identity. Injectivity is unnecessary, and Matrix.of selects the intended matrix construction.
